searchDocs.title: Introduction
searchDocs.content: Introduction This guide describes the requirements and steps needed for integrating with PayPay for customers who wish to integrate our payment services directly into their applications. Methods are provided for: Payment reference generation: payable via our website or online banking/ATM;Simplified checkout payment: offers multiple payment methods via the website;Direct payment with specified payment method – e.g.: Payment via mobile number MB WAY or registered card (tokenisation);POS payment (terminal/TPA): in-person payments with credit/debit card using contactless or Chip and PIN on Cloud terminals, with real-time transaction communication to PayPay,Payment status notification: receive real-time events about changes in the payment status.

searchDocs.title: Standalone Terminal​
searchDocs.content: Autonomous solution ideal for businesses that need a quick and simple way to accept payments.   When to use:  Physical stores without an integrated management system;Points of sale that only need to process payments;Businesses that value simplicity and speed;Businesses that do not require integration with external software.  Features:  Plug & play setup: no technical configuration required;Automatic real-time synchronization with the PayPay backoffice;Optional webhook for transaction notifications;Fully autonomous operation;Ideal for quickly starting to accept payments.

searchDocs.title: Cloud Terminal​
searchDocs.content: Advanced solution for businesses that need full integration between terminals and management systems.   When to use:  E-commerce with a physical store that requires omnichannel integration;POS systems that need to initiate payments remotely;Invoicing software with integrated payments;Restaurants with order management systems;Full automation of sales and payment processes.  Features:  Remote communication with the terminal to initiate a transaction (no manual entry of amount);Real-time bidirectional synchronization;Webhook for automatic transaction confirmation in your system;Full integration with third-party software;Ideal for automation and an optimized user experience.

searchDocs.content: Contactless: Bring the card or mobile device close to the terminal.Chip: Insert the card with chip.Magnetic stripe: Swipe the card (where applicable).

searchDocs.title: 1. Card Presentation​
searchDocs.content: When the operator enters the amount to be paid on the terminal (for standalone terminals) or sends the remote request to the terminal (for cloud terminals), the customer must:  present the card using one of the following methods: Contactless: Bring the card or mobile device close to the terminal.Chip: Insert the card into the terminal.Magnetic stripe: Swipe the card. The terminal reads the card data.

searchDocs.title: 2. Authentication​
searchDocs.content: Depending on the amount and the type of card, authentication may be required:  The card data is read by the terminal.The system checks whether authentication is required: If yes: The customer enters the PIN. If the PIN is correct: proceed with authorisation.If the PIN is incorrect: retry or cancel (max. 3 attempts). If not: Direct processing for authorisation.  Authentication types:  PIN: For transactions above the contactless limit.Signature: For some card types (less common).No authentication: For low-value contactless payments.

searchDocs.title: 3. Processing and Authorisation​
searchDocs.content: The terminal communicates with the payment network to authorise the transaction:  Data validated on the terminal (secure and encrypted connection);The terminal sends the request to the payment network;The network contacts the issuing bank for validation;The bank checks available funds and card limits;The response is sent back to the terminal: Approved: Transaction authorised and debit completed.Declined: Error message displayed.  information The authorisation process usually takes 2–5 seconds.

searchDocs.title: 4. Confirmation and Receipt​
searchDocs.content: After authorisation, the payment is completed:  Transaction approved by the bank;The transaction is automatically synchronised in real time with the PayPay backoffice;PayPay checks that the webhook is configured: If yes: The notification is sent to the external system.If not: The transaction is only visible in the backoffice.

searchDocs.title: 1. When do payments change to the "Confirmed" status?​
searchDocs.content: Payments from Verifone terminals only change to the Confirmed after PayPay receives the settlement with a successful operation status.  information Settlement is the financial clearing process that definitively confirms the transaction with the acquiring bank.

searchDocs.title: 2. What happens if a transaction is successfully completed on a Cloud terminal but the webhook does not reach PayPay in time?​
searchDocs.content: The behaviour depends on the payment expiry date and the configuration sent:   📋 Scenario 1: Valid date still active​  Result: The payment is accepted and changes to Authorised.  📋 Scenario 2: Expired date, but payment within grace period​  Result: The payment is accepted and remains in Authorised (Cancelled).  📋 Scenario 3: Expired date + flag blockLatePayment enabled​  Condition: The payment request included the flag "validDate": {"blockLatePayment": true}.Result: The payment is voided and remains in Cancelled, even if the payment date is within the validity period.  Request Example:  { "amount": 100, "validDate": { "blockLatePayment": true } }   📋 Scenario 4: Expired date and payment outside grace period​  Result: The payment is void and remains in Cancelled.

searchDocs.title: 3. Once a payment is in "Settled" status, what is the maximum time to process a refund?​
searchDocs.content: There is no maximum period to process refunds for payments in "Settled" status.  information There is no maximum time to process refunds, but doing so promptly helps maintain efficient financial management and improves the customer experience.

searchDocs.content: Payment of the purchase To purchase a product/service, the customer must log in to the WooCommerce store. Add items to your cart. To confirm the purchase, click 'Checkout'. After completing the delivery information, select the payment type (ATM, Credit/Debit Card, or MB WAY). information Payment method settings must be defined in the PayPay customer area. You can also set minimum and maximum amounts for different payment methods to gain better control over limits. When selecting the 'ATM' option, a payment reference for the exact order amount is generated. In this area, you can view the summary of your purchase. By accessing the order history, you can view the details of the order you just placed. In the details of your last order, you can see the payment reference generated by PayPay. If the customer has selected the 'Credit/Debit Card' payment option, they must enter their card details and confirm the payment. information Your store will send the payment information to your customers via email. When paying via the 'MB WAY' option, enter the mobile phone number associated with the MB WAY account. After these steps, a payment alert will be sent to the associated number. In the app, authorize the payment and enter the MB WAY PIN. Once the payment is complete, click 'Update'.
